title: Sets and Unique Collections
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of sets and unique collections in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply sets and unique collections in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to version and loading considerations and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Sets and Unique Collections through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding sets and unique collections helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Sets and Unique Collections helps you reason about the set collection. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: The Set collection. Then connect it to Membership testing. The remaining syllabus points—Union, intersection, and difference, Version and loading considerations—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Example: Sets and Unique Collections
content_blocks.code:

a = Set[1, 2, 3]
b = Set[3, 4]
